- When sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., < 0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to recent highs.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.4–0.7), model frequently overreacts to short-term volatility; apply 1–2 day lag correction or use 14-day SMA for smoothing.
- When sentiment is high (e.g., >0.6), model often underestimates upside; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if recent 7-day mean is rising.
- Model tends to overforecast in early 30-day window if sentiment is volatile; use 10-day rolling median instead of 30-day average for initial 10–15 days.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model often fails to adjust; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment drop (e.g., -0.1 * sentiment change).
